newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips start to come under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips start to come under pressure.

text.p: Large volumes of blue chip shares were on offer on the Nigerian stock exchange on Monday, although the index closed little changed in moderate trade, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6570.52 from 6570.28.

Traders said investors were keen to take profits from recent gains at some of Nigeria's largest companies, but were having difficulty finding buyers at current prices and were reluctant to sell for less.

Apparently immune were oil marketing companies, which continued to prosper. Total closed at 47.50 naira, up 35 kobo. African Petroleum, National Oil and Uniptrol gained 20 kobo each to close at 32.82 naira, 34.20 naira and 41.80 naira respectively.
Nestle Foods rose 20 kobo to 33.60 naira. Union Dicon Salt closed up 20 kobo at 35.80 naira.
Benue Cement finished 20 kobo higher at 7.20 naira.
Shares in some smaller banks gained, but the big players were left unmoved. NAL Merchant Bank gained 10 kobo to 5.10 naira.
Cadbury came under early pressure but settled to 26.70 by the close.
Tyre maker Dunlop was down 20 kobo to 11.30 naira. Vitafoam fell 20 kobo to 4.40 naira.
Guinness dropped 15 kobo to 8.09 naira and Nigerian Breweries was 10 kobo lower at 12.10 naira.
PZ Industries went ex-dividend, down 30 kobo at 35.70 naira.
